sections.h2: What kind of city is Richmond, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Richmond is the seat of Madison County, set in the Bluegrass region about 26 miles south of Lexington and 110 miles southeast of Louisville, according to the city's own site. Colonel John Miller founded it in 1798 and named it for his birthplace in Virginia, and it was incorporated in 1809. The Kentucky River forms the county's northern edge, and the city spreads over roughly 19 to 20 square miles.

History matters to housing here. Confederate forces won the Battle of Richmond on August 30, 1862, and a normal school opened in 1906 that grew into Eastern Kentucky University. After rapid growth in the late 1990s and early 2000s, Richmond became the seventh largest city in Kentucky. A house in Richmond is often a few blocks from either a Civil War landmark or a campus.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Richmond housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the city at 40,663 people for July 2025, up from a 2020 base of 35,164, spread over 15,202 households of about 2.17 people. Growth that quick pulls demand toward both rentals and starter homes.

Fewer than four in ten households own, a low share compared with most Kentucky cities. Many Richmond houses are therefore rentals, and a seller with tenants in place should expect buyers to ask for leases and rent rolls.

sections.h2: How does Eastern Kentucky University affect selling a house in Richmond?
sections.html:
The university gives Richmond a young population. The 2020 census recorded a median age of 29.1 years, and 37.4 percent of households were one person living alone. Student demand supports rentals near campus, while families and staff buy farther out toward the bypass.

An owner who inherited a rental, or who is tired of managing one, can sell with tenants, wait out a lease, or close with a buyer who takes over the lease. Check the lease end date before you accept any offer, since a vacant house usually shows better and sells faster.

sections.h2: Which city permit and code rules can complicate a Richmond sale?
sections.html:
Richmond's building inspection office (859-625-6428) enforces the 2018 Kentucky Building Code and related standards. If a prior owner finished a basement, added a deck or swapped a furnace without paperwork, the gap can surface during a buyer's inspection.

  • Permits are required for new construction, structural additions, basement remodels that change the occupant load, and room additions.
  • Sheds and garages need a permit at 200 square feet or larger in residential zones.
  • Decks and porches need one at 200 square feet or larger, 30 inches or more above grade, roofed, or attached to the dwelling.
  • Furnace, air conditioner and electrical panel replacements need permits, and electrical and HVAC installers who are not the homeowner need a city business license.
  • Exterior work inside the H1 historic district goes before the Architectural Review Board, and ground mounted solar is not allowed in residential sections.

Codes Enforcement applies the International Property Maintenance Code and meets as a board on the second Wednesday of each month at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 239 W. Main Street. Call 859-625-6404 about an open case before you list.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and neighborhoods compare around Richmond?
sections.html:
Interstate 75 runs along the west side with three exits, and U.S. 25 and 421 form the eastern bypass toward Lexington. State Route 876 loops around the business district. Berea is about 14 miles south on U.S. 25. The Blue Grass Army Depot lies southeast of the city, and a CSX line runs north and south through town.

  • Madison County Schools serves the city, since the old Richmond district merged into it in 1988.
  • Elementary schools include Daniel Boone, Glenn Marshall, Kit Carson and White Hall, plus Madison Kindergarten Academy.
  • Middle schools are Madison Middle, B. Michael Caudill and Clark Moores, and Madison Central is the main high school.
  • Model Laboratory School is tied to the university.

Summers are hot and humid and winters mild to cool, so buyers focus on HVAC age more than snow loads.

sections.h2: How are Madison County property taxes billed and paid in Richmond?
sections.html:
The Madison County Sheriff takes payments at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, by mail, or through an online portal, Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 4:30. Call 859-623-1511 with questions. Homestead and disability exemptions go through the Madison County PVA at 859-623-5410. The city's finance page says card and online payment is available for city property taxes.

State law makes the tax a personal debt of whoever owned the property on the January 1 assessment date (KRS 134.015). Paying in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the face amount is due through December 31, and later payments carry 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. In practice, buyers and sellers split the year's tax at closing, and the sheriff's office points out that the current owner remains responsible for making sure the bill is paid.

sections.h2: Is it too late to appeal a Richmond property assessment?
sections.html:
For 2026 it is. Under KRS 133.045 the tax roll opens for inspection for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, with Saturday hours, and a taxpayer must talk to the PVA before filing an appeal. That window ended in May 2026 and returns next spring.

A seller planning to list soon can still use the same logic. Bring recent comparable sales to the PVA and ask the office to explain how the value was calculated. If your value is above what recent neighbors sold for, correcting it lowers your carrying cost for the next owner too.

sections.h2: What costs does a seller face at a Richmond closing?
sections.html: Kentucky's deed transfer tax lands on the seller at 50 cents per $500 of price (KRS 142.050). On a sale at the city's typical $214,900 value, the tax is $215.00. Add the prorated property tax, any payoff of a mortgage or lien, and any commission if you hire an agent. Selling to a cash buyer removes the commission and repair costs from the list, but compare the price carefully.

faqs.q: Does Richmond require a permit to replace a furnace?
faqs.a: Yes. Heating and air conditioning replacements are on the city's permit list, and the work must pass inspection. Call the Building Inspection office at 859-625-6428 before a contractor starts, since a missing permit can surface when a buyer orders an inspection.
A large share is. Only 38.3 percent of households own their homes, according to Census QuickFacts, so rentals make up the majority of occupied housing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Madison County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Madison County Sheriff at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, by mail or through the online tax portal. The office phone is 859-623-1511, and hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Richmond house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A seller can sell a house with open code issues, but the city's Codes Enforcement office should be contacted first at 859-625-6404. Its board meets the second Wednesday of each month, and an unresolved case is easier to discuss with a buyer if you know the current status.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I owe selling in Richmond?
faqs.a: The tax is 50 cents per $500 of the sale price, paid by the seller. A $214,900 sale owes $215.00 because each $500 or fraction counts as a unit. Exemptions apply to foreclosure deeds and some family transfers.
